name: Polypodium leucotomos
short: 2015 review of 19 human studies (route not given for each): side effects (stomach or bowel complaints, itching) mild to moderate, in 16 of 1016 people; no dedicated safety studies existed then.
text: A 2015 review that searched for randomised trials of Polypodium leucotomos extract and included 19 human and 6 laboratory studies over 40 years found side effects (gastrointestinal complaints and itching) in 16 of 1016 people (2%), all mild to moderate, and no adverse effects in the laboratory studies. The abstract refers to extracts applied to the skin or taken by mouth and reports oral daily doses of 120 mg to 1080 mg, but does not say which route each human study used; the authors noted that no articles had then been published specifically evaluating its safety, and concluded that it was well tolerated with a negligible risk of side effects. In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in healthy adults taking the extract by mouth twice daily for 60 days, there were no changes in any safety assessment, which included physical examination, vital signs, blood counts, a metabolic panel and blood clotting times; the abstract does not give the number of participants. A 2025 systematic review of 21 studies of the oral extract in skin conditions described an encouraging safety profile. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
